$comment: The Granular Reverb's parameters, declared once.
Both the C++ dispatch and the TypeScript control table are generated from
this file, for the reason fx-01's manifest gives: a parity check between two
hand-maintained tables is a test that passes for a long time and then fails
once, after the drift has shipped.
Every `apply` body here is a single setter, which is unusual among these
manifests and is worth saying why. The reverb's interactions are enforced
inside the unit rather than at the dispatch — the pitch set clamps the
damping corner, the minimum offset is clamped against the grain length, the
decay is inverted through a measured table. §3.3 asks for an unstable
shimmer to be unreachable rather than warned about, and a clamp that lives in
the setter is unreachable from every caller, including a preset load and an
automation lane. A dispatch that reproduced those rules would be a second
Pre-delay sync is stepped in quarter notes rather than free, because the
values that are musically useful are a short list and a continuous control
would let a user land between two of them — a synced delay that is nearly a
sixteenth is worse than an unsynced one, since it beats against the material

params.name: Mix
params.note: Zero must null exactly, which §9 V1 measures at −360 dBFS — an equal-power law that only approached zero would not.

params.name: Pre-delay
params.note: Ahead of the buffer, so it delays what the cloud reads rather than what the cloud produces.

params.name: Size
params.note: Sets the mean read offset with Min offset, and the decay calibration is indexed by that mean — which is why reverb_decay.h takes it as an argument rather than assuming a size.

params.name: Min offset
params.note: Clamped hard: below a grain length the grains read the write head and the loop self-oscillates. §6 says clamp rather than warn, and an unreachable state is better than a documented one.

params.name: Decay
params.note: Inverted through reverb_decay.h's measured table rather than §2.2's formula, which is inference. §9 V5 grades the result over an ensemble of seeds.

params.name: Freeze
params.note: Stops the write head. §2.4 rules out setting the feedback to one, and §9 V11 is the row that tells the two apart.

params.name: Grain size
params.note: Below 15 ms the window itself colours the sound; the face marks that point rather than preventing it.

params.name: Density
params.note: With grain size this sets the overlap, which predicts both the sound and the CPU. §9 V13 measures that the cost really is linear in it.

params.name: Spray
params.note: Randomises where in the size window each grain reads.

params.name: Onset jitter
params.note: Zero makes the grain rate audible as a tone; the default trades that for the occasional gap at low overlap, which is what GE-04 records.

params.name: Length jitter
params.note: Widens the distribution of live grains, which is what the pool's 256 slots are sized against.

params.name: Amp jitter
params.note: Per-grain gain variation. It does not change the cloud's mean level, because the normalisation is applied at spawn.

params.name: Window shape
params.note: Hann at zero, and the Tukey table is a phase remap of the Hann one so that end is bit-exact rather than merely close.

params.name: Pitch set
params.note: A non-unison set clamps the damping corner and the blocker, so an unstable shimmer is unreachable rather than warned about (§3.3).

params.name: Pitch spread
params.note: Per-grain detune on top of the set.

params.name: Diffusion
params.note: Drives the loop's allpass chain. It does not move §9 V7's echo density, because that row measures the first arrivals and the chain is inside the loop — the ledger records why it stays there.

params.name: Damping
params.note: Lower-bounded by the pitch set, so a shimmer cannot be undamped into a runaway.

params.name: Tilt
params.note: Compounds per pass, so a small setting is a large tail.

params.name: Width
params.note: Mid/side on the wet bus only, so a mono dry stays mono.

params.name: Output trim
params.note: After the wet/dry mix, so it trims the whole unit rather than the tail.

params.name: Quality
params.note: Caps the overlap and selects the interpolation. GE-11 publishes what Eco costs in alias floor rather than hiding it.

params.name: Bypass
params.note: A bypassed unit is still in circuit and still meters, which is what X24 found four units getting wrong.

params.name: Pre-delay sync
params.note: Quarter notes; zero leaves Pre-delay in milliseconds, which is what every row written before this one used. §6 lists the option and the tempo comes from the host per block rather than from the map, so the unit keeps no second opinion about where the song is.
